explanation: Switzerland hosted and won the first contest, held in Lugano in 1956 with seven countries. Glastonbury began in 1970, when a £1 ticket included free milk from the farm.

claims.text: The first Eurovision Song Contest was held in Lugano, Switzerland, on 24 May 1956.
The first Glastonbury Festival was held at Worthy Farm, Pilton, in September 1970.
Seven countries took part in the first Eurovision Song Contest, which Switzerland won.
Tickets for the first Glastonbury Festival cost £1 and included free milk from the farm.

issues.note: Label b, 'The first Glastonbury Festival', has a literal second reading: the composer Rutland Boughton ran a series called the Glastonbury Festival in the town of Glastonbury from 1914 to 1926, which would put Glastonbury before 1956 and flip the key. The modern festival is the overwhelming reading and the reveal shows 'September 1970', so this is a note; a qualifier such as 'The first Glastonbury at Worthy Farm' (36 characters) would close it.
